title: The Rust Programming Language
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The canonical guided tour. This curriculum follows its chapter order so every module has an authoritative long-form counterpart.

title: Rust by Example
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Runnable snippets for the same concepts. Use it when you want to see the shape of the code before reading the argument for it.

title: Rustlings
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Small compiler-error-driven fixes. Closest external analogue to this app's terminal work; good for extra repetitions.

title: The Rust Standard Library
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Primary API reference. Every collection, trait, and guarantee named in a lesson is specified here first.

title: The Rust Reference
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Language-level specification. Reach for it when you need the rule rather than an explanation of the rule.

title: The rustc Error Index
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: One page per E-code with a minimal reproduction and repair. The compiler-error nodes in the concept map link straight here.

title: The Cargo Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Manifest keys, profiles, workspaces, features, and publishing. The authority behind every cargo command this app runs.

title: The Edition Guide
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: What changed across 2015/2018/2021/2024. Read it before trusting an older blog post or Stack Overflow answer.

title: Comprehensive Rust
author: Google
blurb: A dense multi-day course with speaker notes, plus bare-metal, Android, and Chromium tracks the Book never covers.

title: The Rust Cookbook
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Task-shaped recipes using well-known crates. Useful once you know the language and need the ecosystem's default answer.

title: Rust Design Patterns
author: rust-unofficial
blurb: Idioms, patterns, and named anti-patterns. The vocabulary layer between 'it compiles' and 'a reviewer would accept it'.

title: Effective Rust
author: David Drysdale
blurb: Thirty-five specific pieces of advice on types, traits, dependencies, and tooling. Commercially published, so this app links to it and never reproduces it.

title: Rust API Guidelines
author: The Rust Library Team
blurb: The checklist library authors are held to: naming, interoperability, flexibility, future proofing.

title: The Rustonomicon
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The dark arts of unsafe Rust: aliasing, variance, drop order, and the invariants you now have to uphold by hand.

title: Learn Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists
author: Aria Beingessner
blurb: The best available treatment of ownership under pressure. Work it after Chapter 15; it turns smart pointers into muscle memory.

title: Rust Atomics and Locks
author: Mara Bos
blurb: Free online edition covering memory ordering, building your own locks, and what the OS actually does underneath.

title: Asynchronous Programming in Rust
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Futures, executors, pinning, and cancellation from first principles rather than from one runtime's API surface.

title: Tokio Tutorial
author: The Tokio Contributors
blurb: The concrete counterpart to the async book: tasks, channels, select, shared state, and graceful shutdown in a real runtime.

title: The Little Book of Rust Macros
author: Veykril (community edition)
blurb: macro_rules! from fragment specifiers to hygiene, then the bridge into procedural macros.

title: The Rust Performance Book
author: Nicholas Nethercote
blurb: Profiling first, then measured wins: allocation, hashing, bounds checks, build configuration, and benchmarking discipline.

title: Rust Quiz
author: David Tolnay
blurb: Short programs with surprising output and a full explanation. Excellent calibration for how well you actually read Rust.

title: TheAlgorithms / Rust
author: TheAlgorithms community
blurb: Reference implementations for classic algorithms in idiomatic-ish Rust. Compare against your own after you have solved a pattern.

title: Exercism Rust Track
author: Exercism
blurb: Around a hundred graded exercises with published community solutions — the widest source of alternative idiom for a solved problem.
